clue.text: Changed-off one's rocker, maybe?

definitions.meaning: altered or adjusted in some way
a rocker (a 1960s motorbike youth) turned into a Mod, the rival tribe, has been made a Mod

explanation.walkthrough: Mods and Rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s, so someone no longer a rocker might have been turned Mod. 'Off one's rocker' wants to mean mad, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered or adapted has been changed, and the playful second sense reads the word as 'turned Mod'.

clue.text: Field marshal known for being ratty?

definitions.text: Field marshal known for being ratty?

parts.words: Field marshal known for being ratty?
parts.note: the British commander of the Eighth Army in North Africa, whose forces included the Desert Rats, so he was associated with rats rather than bad temper

explanation.surface: A senior army officer famous for his irritable temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' suggests bad-tempered; the joke is the Desert Rats, the 7th Armoured Division that fought under this field marshal at El Alamein.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Law, Viscount of Alamein, was the famous British field marshal of the Second World War, nicknamed Monty.

clue.text: Superficial complaint?

parts.note: superficial here means on the surface of the body, so a complaint of the skin rather than a trivial grumble

explanation.walkthrough: 'Superficial complaint' sounds like a shallow grievance, but it means an illness affecting the surface, the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the skin is literally a disorder found on the body's surface.

clue.text: Meat off shelf

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Meat that has gone bad sitting on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like meat gone bad, but it tells you to rearrange SHELF.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft tissue of an animal eaten as food is its meat.

clue.text: Release name falsely used by bogus optician

indicators.note: falsely and bogus both say the letters are not genuine, so name and optician are mixed together into one new word

explanation.surface: A fake eye doctor sets someone free under an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NAME and OPTICIAN together rearrange to give the answer; 'falsely' and 'bogus' both signal the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting people free from slavery or legal restriction is their release.

clue.text: Greek island possibly a hit with chartered accountant

indicators.note: possibly says the following words may be arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: An accountant scores a success on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A HIT into ITHA, and CA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian isle that was home to Odysseus is one of the Greek islands.

clue.text: Timber used to make a figure of eight?

definitions.text: Timber used to make a figure of eight?

parts.words: Timber used to make a figure of eight?
parts.note: a length of wood named for its cross-section in inches, read as a sum: two multiplied by four gives a total of eight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure of eight' suggests a looped shape, but it is the number eight, the product of the two dimensions in the timber's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of sawn lumber measuring two inches by four in section is a standard building timber.

clue.text: Man making a name around Los Angeles

indicators.note: around says the a-plus-name pair is placed on either side of the next piece

explanation.surface: A man making his name in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N go around LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so an example of a man.

clue.text: A lieutenant meets old singer

explanation.surface: A junior officer meets a veteran vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with a low female or high male voice is named after that vocal range.

clue.text: Viking name applied to rider losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the rider word is dropped

parts.note: a horseman is a rider on horseback

explanation.surface: A Viking's name is given to a beheaded horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the H from HORSEMAN to leave ORSEMAN, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were seafaring raiders from Scandinavia, men of the North.

clue.text: Metal company taking on Lithuanian, for instance

parts.note: a Lithuanian is one example of a Balt, a native of a Baltic state

explanation.surface: A metal firm takes on a worker from Lithuania.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard bluish-grey element used in alloys and pigments is a metal.

clue.text: Male equivalent of shocking pink?

parts.note: pink is the traditional colour for girls and blue for boys; shocking pink has a vivid counterpart where shocking is swapped for a word about electricity

explanation.walkthrough: Shocking pink is a vivid colour; swap pink (girls) for blue (boys) and 'shocking' for its electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant steely shade of blue named after the glow of an electric spark.

clue.text: Calligraphy displayed vividly

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fine handwriting put on show in a striking way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' tells you to rearrange CALLIGRAPHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something in clear, vivid detail is describing it in a lifelike, picture-like way.

clue.text: Even in inflationary times this will not rise

definitions.text: Even in inflationary times this will not rise

parts.words: Even in inflationary times this will not rise
parts.note: the surface talks of prices rising with inflation, but the rising meant is dough rising, which a flat unleavened loaf never does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflationary' and 'rise' suggest prices, but this flat Middle Eastern bread is unleavened so it does not rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, unleavened Mediterranean loaf that opens into a pocket does not puff up when baked.

clue.text: Protect friends in nearby taxi stands

parts.note: close means nearby
taxi ranks are where cabs wait for passengers

explanation.surface: Defending your mates at the cab stands nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to unite in mutual defence, as soldiers stood shoulder to shoulder to shield allies.

clue.text: Puzzling place in which to find one American crop

indicators.note: in which to find says the one is placed inside the puzzling place

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle you walk through
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A maze hidden in an American cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside MAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn native to the Americas is a cereal crop.

clue.text: Idea drawn, perhaps,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'Idea drawn, perhaps, (9)': an anagram of IDEA DRAWN with its trailing comma and no defining word, so the definition appears cut off in the OCR text and no search found the rest.

clue.text: Old Scot speaking about one in images

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland

indicators.note: about says the speaking word goes around the one

parts.note: oral means spoken, done by speaking
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot talks about someone in pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: PICT, then ORAL around I gives ORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expressed through pictures is presented visually, in images.

clue.text: It falls in rugged terrain around West Africa

indicators.note: around says the rearranged terrain goes either side of the next piece
rugged suggests something rough and broken up, so the letters of terrain are rearranged

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for West Africa

explanation.surface: Rain pours down over rough ground in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugged' rearranges TERRAIN to RAINTER, which goes around WA.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that has come down from the sky as rain is what falls in a shower.

clue.text: Gives assessment in extra test

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone marks a candidate in an additional exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'extRA TESt'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grade or evaluate something is to give it an assessment.

clue.text: Ivy, typically, offering cheer to mountaineer

parts.note: to root for someone is to cheer them on (American usage)
a mountaineer is a climber

explanation.surface: Ivy encourages a rock climber.
explanation.walkthrough: To root, in American English, is to cheer a team on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy clings to walls using aerial roots, so it is an example of a plant that climbs by roots.

clue.text: Found in certain dictionaries of Sanskrit language group

indicators.note: found in says the letters are inside the following words

explanation.surface: A language family listed in some reference books.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'certaIN DICtionaries'.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of Indo-European including Sanskrit and Hindi is the Indo-Aryan family.

clue.text: One occupying old

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'One occupying old (4)': it gives I (one) and O (old) but no definition and no piece for the rest of the letters, so it looks cut short and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Academic demonstration leaving nothing out

indicators.note: leaving, with out, says the nothing letter is dropped from the demonstration word

parts.note: a proof is a demonstration that something is true
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lecturer's demonstration leaves nothing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving nothing out' drops one O from PROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for professor, a senior university academic.

clue.text: Very nasty state seen in house on road

indicators.note: seen in says the state is placed inside the road

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A dreadful condition in a house on a street.
explanation.walkthrough: HO, then RI inside RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or extremely unpleasant is very nasty.

clue.text: Club bungled badly, receiving nothing

indicators.note: receiving says the rearranged letters take in the nothing piece
badly says the letters of bungled are disordered

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A club bungled a deal badly and got nothing out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges BUNGLED to BLUDGEN, which takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy short stick used as a weapon is a club.

clue.text: Break law -bad way to finish

parts.note: off means bad, as food that has spoiled
an end is the way something finishes

explanation.surface: Breaking the law is a bad way to end things.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit a crime or transgress is to break the law.

clue.text: Appear about to acquire a sort of cred, having foreign car

indicators.note: to acquire says the turned word takes in the rearranged letters
about says the appear word is turned round

parts.note: to seem is to appear

indicators.note: a sort of says the following word is changed into another form

explanation.surface: Wanting to look cool, someone buys a foreign car for street cred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SEEM into MEES, which takes in RCED, a rearrangement of CRED.
explanation.definitionFit: The German luxury marque from Stuttgart makes cars that are foreign to British drivers.
